chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said:

The dhimmi man has a dhimmi wife, so his wife becomes a Muslim. He said: 'She is his wife; he is with her by the day and is not with her by the night.' He said: 'So if the man becomes a Muslim and the wife does not become a Muslim, the man is with her by the night and the day.'

key_terms.الذِّمِّيُّ: A non-Muslim subject living under Islamic rule
key_terms.يَكُونُ عِنْدَهَا: He is with her / cohabits with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marital cohabitation when one spouse is Muslim and the other is a dhimmi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of marital continuity in mixed-faith unions, distinguishing between a non-Muslim wife converting (resulting in nocturnal separation) and a non-Muslim husband converting (allowing full cohabitation). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the husband's conversion does not automatically dissolve the marriage if the wife remains a 'Person of the Book' (Ahl al-Kitab), whereas the wife's conversion to Islam while the husband remains non-Muslim creates a barrier to conjugal relations. This ruling underscores the asymmetry in marital validity based on the gender of the convert in classical Shia fiqh.
